candidate_relations.reason: The reference diagnosis is tumoral calcinosis, a calcium phosphate deposition disorder presenting as periarticular calcified masses. Giant cell tumor of the tendon sheath is a separate benign fibrohistiocytic neoplasm of synovial origin. Although the clinical record describes the working diagnosis as giant cell tumor of the tendon sheath, the benchmark reference specifies tumoral calcinosis as the most likely diagnosis. These are not equivalent entities; tumoral calcinosis would typically show calcified deposits on imaging rather than the vascular multilobulated soft-tissue mass described, but the reference diagnosis must be taken as given.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Giant cell tumor of the tendon sheath vs. tumoral calcinosis — distinct diagnostic entities

case_quality_flags: Discordance between clinical working diagnosis (giant cell tumor of tendon sheath) and reference diagnosis (tumoral calcinosis) is notable; imaging description (multilobulated echogenic mass with vascularity in extensor compartment) is more consistent with giant cell tumor of tendon sheath than tumoral calcinosis, raising a possible reference diagnosis quality concern.
No radiograph or CT was performed to evaluate for calcification, which would be the key discriminating finding for tumoral calcinosis.
